gaps.what: Shapes 644-859, 860, 960-1040, 1099, 1227 and the end year 1235 (south-west Wales and Ayrshire-Galloway) rest on the Cliopatria shape alone; Dunoding (6 cells at 592) and Hwicce (13 cells at 577) have no page.

21 of 28 events are confidence 1: every Cliopatria carve-out into a dedicated row (Welsh rows 540, Rheged 592, Dumnonia 602, Strathclyde 644, Seisyllwg 911/960, Gwynedd 1056/1216, Norman England 1085) and the 480, 587, 617, 628, 936 handovers are undated by the pages opened.
North-west England 870-935 is credited by the Rheged page to Strathclyde (around 900); Cliopatria draws it as Brythons from 870. The strathclyde dossier should carry it.
Elmet 616/617-627, Gododdin to 638, Dyfed, Ceredigion and Galloway have no Cliopatria row or dossier; Elmet is drawn Anglian (Deira) too early.

gaps.what: No infobox area on any page opened, so the factor-of-two check could not be made for any shape.
The 480 growth (144 cells) and the 533/534 hand-over to Mercia, Wessex and Deira are undated by every page opened; Wihtgar (523 vs 534) and the Chronicle dates for Wessex (495, 519) are not covered.

problems: Cliopatria's Brythons is a residual of the Britons' land, not one state: kept as one dossier of type state with no capitals or rulers; the renderers should let the dedicated rows win where they overlap.

The Brythons shapes double-claim land with other rows in Dumnonia 602-611, Mercia 628-632, Seisyllwg 911-935, Gwynedd 1056-1065 and 1216-1226 and Norman England 1094-1098; corrected by new keyframes that override the Cliopatria shape for their own years only.

WebFetch returns a model's summary of each page, so the quotations in notes are the summary's quotations of the page text and were not checked against the raw wikitext; two pages (Sub-Roman Britain, Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain) disagree on the Breton settlement date and the settlement page is silent on the Chronicle dates for Kent, Sussex and Wessex.
sources_total counts the two shared pages (Sub-Roman Britain, Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain) once per dossier: 17 distinct pages in all (14 + 5 - 2).

The anglo-saxon-england dossier carves Kent (c. 455) and Sussex (477) out of the 441-480 shapes; it agrees with the kingdom-of-kent and kingdom-of-sussex dossiers but contradicts Cliopatria's 490 start for both rows.

The kingdom-of-deira dossier of the same group dates Deira to c. 450 (parent anglo-saxon-england) while Cliopatria starts the row in 534 and takes Yorkshire from the Anglo-Saxon England shape; the Hwicce, Wihtwara and Dunoding pages were not opened here.
